# Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 58 (Bi-Vb Pc58)

**ID:** Bi-Vb Pc58
**Section:** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (bi-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 58
**Title (English, from literature):** Not going to the instruction

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 58 (titled *Ovāda*) stipulates that a Buddhist nun who fails to attend the regular instruction (*ovāda*) or the formal meetings of the monastic community commits an offense of expiation requiring confession. According to the analysis of Ute Hüsken, this rule, together with Pācittiya 59, regulates the fortnightly instruction of the nuns' Order by monks as an established communal institution [Hüsken 1997]. Hüsken observes that attendance at this instruction was regarded primarily as a privilege for a nun and that the rule presupposes the existing institutionalization of the *ovāda*, likely postdating the corresponding Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga rules governing the instruction of nuns (Bhikkhu Pācittiya 21–24) [Hüsken 1997]. The commentary (*Samantapāsādikā*) indicates that the content of the instruction comprised Vinaya regulations and training rules [Hüsken 1997].

 A passage-level parallel is also found in the *Bhikkhunikkhandhaka* of the Cullavagga (Kd 20). DharmaNexus identifies substantial Pali-internal formulaic text reuse across 68 texts, sharing longest contiguous segments with Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Saṅghādisesa 3 (§1.6–1.14.1), Pācittiya 57 (§1.6–2.1.4), Pācittiya 95, and Pācittiya 10, alongside Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 23 (§0.5–1.7) [DharmaNexus]. An English translation has been prepared by Bhikkhu Brahmali.
